# silolink_session_control_tool

> Inspect or control an existing SiloLink (Claude Code) session.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `developer`, `silolink` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=silolink_session_control_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Inspect or control an existing SiloLink (Claude Code) session.

Use this BEFORE reporting progress on a spawned session — never claim
a session is "working on" something without a successful peek in the
last 60 seconds.

Actions:
- `peek`     — capture the last N lines of the session's tmux pane.
               Synchronous (~5s wait). Returns literal output.
- `stop`     — kill the session and unregister it. Terminal.
- `interrupt`— send Esc to the session without killing it. Useful
               when Claude is stuck on an irrelevant prompt.
- `nudge`    — wake an idle session by enqueuing a system message.

`conversation_id` is required for stop / interrupt / nudge — these
target a specific session. For `peek`, omitting both
`conversation_id` and `agent_session_id` peeks all sessions on the
daemon (rarely what you want as an agent — pass conversation_id).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | Control action to perform on the session. One of: `peek`, `status`, `stop`, `interrupt`, `nudge`. |
| `conversation_id` | integer | no | Target SiloLink conversation id. Required for stop/interrupt/nudge. Strongly recommended for peek. |
| `agent_session_id` | integer | no | Optional AgentSession id. Use when you have it; otherwise pass conversation_id. |
| `lines` | integer | no | peek only: number of tmux lines to capture (default 50, max 200). |
| `wait_seconds` | integer | no | peek only: how long to wait for the daemon response, in seconds (default 5, max 10). |
